script: A government hid its own massacre for over thirty years, and blamed the victims instead. In October 1968, thousands of Mexican students gathered peacefully in Tlatelolco Square, days before the Olympics began in Mexico City. Government snipers took position on rooftops overlooking the square. Without warning, they opened fire directly into the crowd. Officials rushed to a podium and claimed the students had attacked police first, reporting only four deaths. That same night, trucks quietly loaded covered bodies away under the cover of darkness. A foreign journalist secretly counted the bodies, certain the real number was being hidden. The truth stayed locked away in classified military archives for over thirty years. In 2001, those files were finally declassified, and historians confirmed hundreds had been killed. The government that once blamed the victims was forced to admit it had lied for three decades.

title: Mexico Hid This Massacre for 33 Years, Then Blamed the Students
description:
In 1968, Mexican government forces opened fire on peaceful student protesters in Tlatelolco Square days before the Olympics. Officials claimed only 4 died and blamed the students. Declassified files in 2001 confirmed hundreds were killed.

Did you know this stayed hidden for over 30 years? Let me know in the comments.
